inspections.finding: The initial kaf has a broad opaque footer and a compact fused downward rectangular swelling. A single absorbed point, contracted bar/stem or ordinary enlarged terminal remains a live competitor; the complete glyph and local single-button/qamats controls do not uniquely certify a vowel or its absence.

The complete mem below its ordinary broad footer carries two vertical rounded expansions separated by a narrower neck. The same-unit mem in שמלתה shows the same pair below its separate footer, while the detached mem sheva in אמללים on page171 independently fixes the two-dot class. The target does not have the horizontal top bar and single lower stem of qamats, horizontal pair of tsere, shallow bar of patah or single compact button of local hiriq. The joined vertical pair is sufficient without requiring white separation. Append U+05B0 after the existing mem; no expected spelling or grammar supplies the mark.

The complete middle cluster is preserved, but the legacy narrow crop labeled shin instead shows an ayin-like two-head form. Its exact correspondence to canonical letterIndex3 and associated lower appendage is not established independently. No point can safely be assigned from that label or inferred from the canonical spelling; retain the note and all existing scalars.

The legacy narrow crop labeled ayin contains a one-head dotted body rather than an independently established exact canonical ayin. The full middle cluster and entire word disclose the uncertainty without selecting a replacement consonant or assigning its visible lower mass to this canonical letter. Retain this disclosure.

The legacy narrow crop labeled nun and the adjacent dotted one-head body leave the exact assignment to canonical letterIndex5 unresolved. A qamats-like lower shape in this cluster cannot retire the note until its point-to-letter correspondence is certified. Keep the complete cluster, current nun dagesh, all other scalars and this disclosure.
